title: The Part That Remains
teaser: Serving as first assistant on an elective open left hepatectomy, Ryuji Sakaguchi witnesses Artoria Pendragon's top-tier hepatobiliary blade and surgical philosophy firsthand.
gallery_caption: Standing across the operating table from Artoria Pendragon during an open left hepatectomy, Sakaguchi learns why protecting the liver that remains matters just as much as what is resected.

choices.choice_ar2_c1_a: "Along the mid-portion of the middle hepatic vein, there's a tributary draining the right anterior sector sitting closer to the left than usual."
choices.choice_ar2_c1_b: "Portal perfusion and biliary confluence in the right hemiliver look full; everything hinges on keeping outflow through the middle hepatic vein intact."
choices.choice_ar2_c1_c: "...Fair point. I was so focused on taking the lesion out cleanly that I didn't calculate the venous outflow margin for the right anterior sector."
choices.choice_ar2_c2_a: Fine-tune left-sided traction tension and drip-suction angle proactively to expose the tributary's outer wall under zero tension.
choices.choice_ar2_c2_b: Coordinate with the ultrasound probe to mark an arc of tiny electrocautery guide points along the cut surface, aligning the deep turn depth with her.
choices.choice_ar2_c2_c: Anticipate the tiny crossing side branches ahead after the turn and pre-align fine vascular sutures and micro-forceps handoffs with Miyuki Asakura.
choices.choice_ar2_c3_a: "A certain lead surgeon taught me ten minutes ago that 'the functional reserve left behind needs protection too'—does the deputy chief's own reserve not count?"
choices.choice_ar2_c3_b: "The cafeteria's probably closed at this hour, though the first-floor kiosk still stocks hot sandwiches. I'm heading down anyway—want me to grab you one?"
choices.choice_ar2_c3_c: "That cup of black tea by your hand has been stone cold since morning. Tea alone won't carry you through afternoon ward rounds."

nodes.ar2_s1_01: Afternoon sunlight slanted across the windowsill of the third-floor surgical ward.
nodes.ar2_s1_02: Twenty-five-year-old Taiga Fujimura sat cross-legged in the middle of her hospital bed, holding her freshly signed copy of the preoperative briefing sheet and eyeing the liver diagram from one angle after another. Hearing the knock at the door, she tucked the sheet beside her knee, straightened her back, and flashed the same boisterous, openhearted grin she wore when coaching students at her kendo dojo:
nodes.ar2_s1_03: "Come right in! Oh, it's Dr. Artoria—and Dr. Sakaguchi came along too!"
nodes.ar2_s1_04: Walking in front, Artoria Pendragon paused to the right of the bed, her pale golden hair gathered at the nape of her neck into an immaculate low chignon, not a single stray crease at the collar or cuffs of her white coat. She gave a slight nod, her voice clear and gentle:
nodes.ar2_s1_05: "Good afternoon, Ms. Fujimura. Before your evening fasting begins, Dr. Sakaguchi—who will be serving as first assistant tomorrow—and I came by to check on you again. Does your upper abdomen still feel full and tight today?"
nodes.ar2_s1_06: Taiga patted just to the right of her solar plexus, still trying out of habit to crack a joke:
nodes.ar2_s1_07: "Haha, to tell you two doctors the truth, just thinking about a benign nodule the size of a fist shoving my stomach crooked—so I can barely finish half a bowl of my favorite pork cutlet rice—makes me wish Dr. Artoria could evict it first thing tomorrow morning!"
nodes.ar2_s1_08: Standing at the foot of the bed checking the chart indicators, Ryuji Sakaguchi offered a warm smile:
nodes.ar2_s1_09: "Good spirits are always welcome. Looking over your coagulation profile and hepatic functional reserve just now, your baseline really is sturdier than most people's."
nodes.ar2_s1_10: Taiga started to arch her eyebrows with pride, only for her gaze to drift inadvertently back to the briefing diagram beside her hand, where a dashed line divided the left and right lobes of the liver.
nodes.ar2_s1_11: All at once, that bravado seemed to lose half a beat of air.
nodes.ar2_s1_12: She rubbed the tip of her nose as the fingers resting on her knees slowly tightened, her voice dropping half a register with the unmistakable apprehension of an adult facing major organ resection:
nodes.ar2_s1_13: "...Speaking honestly though, Dr. Artoria. I took another look at this diagram just now... This whole big piece on the left is coming out—that's nearly half my liver, isn't it?"
nodes.ar2_s1_14: She looked up at the blonde surgeon beside her bed, the teasing fading from her eyes and giving way to undisguised worry:
nodes.ar2_s1_15: "Doctor... After cutting away a piece that big, will I really be okay afterward? Back at the dojo... will I still be able to swing a shinai and live normally like before?"
nodes.ar2_s1_16: Silence settled over the room for a moment.
nodes.ar2_s1_17: Artoria neither brushed her off with glib platitudes like "don't overthink it, everything is guaranteed," nor rushed to overwhelm her with a string of cold percentages.
nodes.ar2_s1_18: Walking calmly to the bedside, she reached out to turn the liver diagram upright. Her slender fingertip did not land first on the shaded lesion on the left, but rested steadily over the wide expanse of clean hepatic parenchyma on the right:
nodes.ar2_s1_19: "Ms. Fujimura, when such a large portion of an organ is being removed from your body, feeling uneasy is completely natural."
nodes.ar2_s1_20: "Please remember one thing, however—what we step up to the operating table to do tomorrow is not merely to cut away the part that has a problem."
nodes.ar2_s1_21: Her gaze was bright and sincere, every word falling clearly upon the patient's ears:
nodes.ar2_s1_22: "The part that remains is just as much what this operation is meant to protect."
nodes.ar2_s1_25: "Yes. Preoperative imaging and hepatic reserve testing have already confirmed that the volume and metabolic compensatory capacity of your healthy right liver are more than sufficient to sustain a normal life—provided that while removing the lesion on the left, we preserve intact arterial and portal venous inflow, unobstructed venous outflow, and free biliary drainage in the liver that stays behind."
nodes.ar2_s1_26: "So long as those structures are protected intact on the table tomorrow, after proper postoperative recovery you will return to the dojo and take up your shinai again. Nothing about it will be a makeshift compromise."
nodes.ar2_s1_27: There was not a single exaggerated chest-thumping promise, yet solid anatomy and physiology underpinned every word.
nodes.ar2_s1_28: Listening in quiet awe, Taiga uncurled her fingers bit by bit from the corner of her blanket; the tips of her ears turned faintly pink with embarrassment before a grounded, reassured smile returned to her face:
nodes.ar2_s1_29: "...Hearing you put it like that, Dr. Artoria, it almost feels like the right half of my liver is puffing out its chest too! Alright—tomorrow, whether it's the part coming out or the part staying behind, I'm leaving all of it in both of your hands!"
nodes.ar2_s1_30: A faint, poised trace of a smile touched the corner of Artoria's lips:
nodes.ar2_s1_31: "Please get plenty of rest. We will see you in the operating room tomorrow morning."
nodes.ar2_s1_32: Stepping out of the ward and pulling the door shut behind them, Sakaguchi turned that brief preoperative exchange over in his mind and gave a quiet inward nod.
nodes.ar2_s1_33: Guiding a patient naturally from fear over "how much is being lost" to peace of mind over "what is being kept"—that calm, measured persuasiveness was genuinely impressive; yet at that moment, Sakaguchi had not fully realized just how much weight words that sounded like bedside reassurance would carry beneath the shadowless lamps the next day.
nodes.ar2_s2_01: Although as Deputy Chief of Surgery she had a private office of her own, Artoria, as always, preferred to work right out in the surgical doctors' office where she could keep track of the entire department at a glance.
nodes.ar2_s2_02: At five-thirty in the evening, the four-panel fluorescent viewing box along one wall snapped bright. Artoria clipped Taiga Fujimura's arterial-, portal-, and delayed-phase contrast CT films onto the lightbox in strict slice order, then turned toward Sakaguchi as he walked over:
nodes.ar2_s2_03: "For tomorrow morning's open hepatic lobectomy, I will be lead surgeon, and I would like you at first assistant, Dr. Sakaguchi. While the office is quiet, let us run through the preoperative imaging together once more."
nodes.ar2_s2_04: Sakaguchi stepped up, his practiced eyes sweeping across the crisp cross-sectional slices on the lightbox.
nodes.ar2_s2_05: To a surgeon with seasoned overseas lead-operating experience, the lesion's relationships on these films were straightforward to read:
nodes.ar2_s2_06: "A large focal hyperplastic lesion in the left hemiliver, straddling the left lateral and left medial sectors, with its inferior margin pushing the lesser curvature of the stomach posteriorly and downward. Fortunately, the pseudocapsule border is clean and doesn't encroach on the main hilar transverse fissure."
nodes.ar2_s2_07: Raising the blunt end of a pencil, he tapped lightly above the first and second porta hepatis on the portal-phase film, laying out his anatomical assessment in clear order:
nodes.ar2_s2_08: "Following a standard anatomical left hepatectomy, there are two main technical cruxes: first, the root of the left Glissonean pedicle sits close to tiny caudate branches, so intrafascial dissection and ligation of the left hepatic artery and left portal vein have to spare the opposite side; second, at the second porta hepatis, the left and middle hepatic veins join in a common trunk entering the inferior vena cava, so dividing the left hepatic vein root demands extra care against bleeding. Lock down both ends cleanly, and taking the left hemiliver en bloc should be straightforward."
nodes.ar2_s2_09: Accurate judgment, clear priorities—by any standard, a textbook answer from an accomplished surgeon.
nodes.ar2_s2_10: Artoria listened quietly until he finished, her emerald-green eyes remarkably pellucid in the cool white glow of the lightbox. She nodded in acknowledgment, yet made no move to take the films down:
nodes.ar2_s2_11: "Your reading of the lesion's borders and the vascular control points on the resected side is entirely accurate."
nodes.ar2_s2_12: Pausing briefly, she glided her slender finger across the midline of the film, pointing toward the right hemiliver where no lesion grew at all:
nodes.ar2_s2_13: "We have already settled the extent of resection."
nodes.ar2_s2_17: "Yes. Just now, while you were reading this film, your gaze stayed fixed on the tissue on the left that is about to leave the patient's body—now shift to the right, and trace the mid-course of the middle hepatic vein once more."
nodes.ar2_s2_18: Narrowing his eyes slightly, Sakaguchi re-examined the three consecutive slices beneath her fingertip.
nodes.ar2_s2_19: Two seconds later, his gaze locked onto an inconspicuous grayish-white vascular shadow along the junction between the right anterior and left medial sectors.
nodes.ar2_c1a_01: Leaning half a step closer, Sakaguchi pointed to a middle slice on the portal-phase film:
nodes.ar2_c1a_02: "The main trunk of the middle hepatic vein itself is clear, but just below its mid-segment, a venous tributary crossing over from the right anterior sector sits noticeably close to the left-right demarcation line at this CT slice thickness."
nodes.ar2_c1a_03: A flicker of approval crossed Artoria's eyes as she gave a slight nod:
nodes.ar2_c1a_04: "Sharp eyes, Dr. Sakaguchi. Because CT slices have spacing, films alone cannot give a final verdict on just how many millimeters separate that vessel from our transection plane—yet it governs venous outflow for that entire expanse of healthy right anterior parenchyma."
nodes.ar2_c1b_01: Sakaguchi traced upward from the right hepatic hilum all the way back to the hepatic venous confluence:
nodes.ar2_c1b_02: "The right hepatic artery, right portal vein, and right hepatic duct confluence all have safe clearance; what really needs watching is making sure the margin of the right anterior sector never turns congested from lost outflow as we divide along the middle hepatic vein."
nodes.ar2_c1b_04: "Precisely. If we preserve inflow while destroying outflow, the parenchyma left behind will still swell, necrose, and even develop bile leaks postoperatively. Seeing the exit on the right clearly is every bit as vital as controlling the entrance on the left."
nodes.ar2_c1c_01: Studying those consecutive slices, Sakaguchi let out a candid breath:
nodes.ar2_c1c_02: "...You got me there, Dr. Artoria. Seeing such a clean pseudocapsule at first glance, my head went straight to how cleanly we could lift out the left hemiliver instead of auditing venous outflow for the right anterior sector first."
nodes.ar2_c1c_03: Without the slightest trace of senior lecturing in her bearing, Artoria answered in a level, candid tone:
nodes.ar2_c1c_04: "Many technically gifted surgeons look at the lesion first—that is only natural. A liver is not an appendix, however: once the resected half goes into the specimen bag, its part is over; the half staying inside the abdomen is what has to carry the patient through the next several decades."
nodes.ar2_s2r_01: Picking up a red-and-blue dual-tipped marker, Artoria sketched tomorrow's baseline plan and verification checkpoints cleanly across the whiteboard diagram beside them:
nodes.ar2_s2r_02: "Tomorrow's plan therefore proceeds in two steps. First, we selectively control left hepatic inflow, set our initial transection line along the surface ischemic demarcation, and keep the main trunk of the middle hepatic vein with the right hemiliver throughout; second, after laparotomy—both before incising the parenchyma and midway through transection—we place the intraoperative ultrasound probe directly onto the liver to verify the true distance to that right anterior tributary and the right hepatic duct."
nodes.ar2_s2r_03: Sakaguchi studied the tightly structured diagram:
nodes.ar2_s2r_04: "Rather than welding the route shut in advance, you leave room for secondary calibration under intraoperative ultrasound?"
nodes.ar2_s2r_05: "A preoperative plan does not exist to prove how accurately the surgeon predicted everything beforehand; it exists so that the moment we see the patient's true anatomy on the table, we know beyond doubt which principles can never yield and which path can adapt."
nodes.ar2_s2r_06: Setting the marker down, she raised her eyes to Sakaguchi, her expression poised yet warm:
nodes.ar2_s2r_07: "Tomorrow's operation calls for patience. I will be counting on your exposure and intraoperative cross-checks from first assistant, Dr. Sakaguchi."
nodes.ar2_s2r_08: Meeting her gaze, Sakaguchi gave a solemn nod:
nodes.ar2_s2r_09: "Understood. See you at the table tomorrow, Dr. Artoria."
nodes.ar2_s3_01: Operating Room One shone bright in the early morning light, fine hilar dissection forceps, atraumatic vascular clamps, graded silk ties, and polypropylene vascular sutures arrayed in crisp ranks across the instrument table while an intraoperative ultrasound unit fitted with a high-frequency T-probe stood ready beside the table.
nodes.ar2_s3_02: In keeping with Hoshimi Hospital's perioperative protocol for major and intermediate open procedures in the ordinary pool, no outside anesthesiologist was assigned to this open hepatic lobectomy; instead, lead surgeon Artoria personally performed high thoracic epidural blockade before scrubbing in.
nodes.ar2_s3_03: At the center of the operating table, twenty-five-year-old Taiga Fujimura—undressed beneath a clean sheet and wearing a light-blue disposable surgical cap—lay curled on her side. Now that antiseptic prep and fenestrated draping were actually underway across her back, even this ordinarily fearless kendo instructor couldn't help bunching a few creases into the edge of her pillow:
nodes.ar2_s3_04: "Ugh... Nurse Anji, was I counting my ECG beeps pushing past a hundred just now...? This needle in my back isn't gonna make me jolt straight off the table, is it?"
nodes.ar2_s3_05: Standing before the table, Anji Tonegawa held her hand and reassured her with earnest warmth:
nodes.ar2_s3_06: "Don't worry, Ms. Fujimura—just keep your back arched nice and steady like a curled-up shrimp without moving. Dr. Artoria's hands are remarkably steady."
nodes.ar2_s3_07: Behind her, Artoria had already donned sterile procedure gloves. Even during preoperative anesthesia placement, not a single step was rushed—raising a thorough local anesthetic skin wheal at the puncture site first, and calmly giving half a second's notice before every needle advance and injection:
nodes.ar2_s3_08: "You will feel a slight dull fullness now. Do not hold your breath—exhale slowly. ...Very good; the epidural catheter is in place."
nodes.ar2_s3_10: "Huh? I-it's already in?! I thought you were just pressing on my back to start!"
nodes.ar2_s3_11: After easing her back supine, administering the test dose, and titrating fractionated local anesthetic alongside mild intravenous sedation to blunt visceral traction reflexes, Artoria brushed an alcohol swab lightly downward from above the xiphoid process—confirming complete loss of pain and temperature sensation from the upper abdomen and costal margins to below the umbilicus, with respiratory muscle strength, blood pressure, and heart rate rock-steady.
nodes.ar2_s3_12: Handing head-side monitoring over to Anji Tonegawa, Artoria leaned slightly toward the visibly relaxed Taiga and spoke gently:
nodes.ar2_s3_13: "The block level is ideal; you will feel no pain during incision or manipulation. Anji will stay right beside your head the entire time—if you feel drowsy, simply close your eyes and rest, and speak up anytime if your chest feels tight or uncomfortable."
nodes.ar2_s3_14: From behind the sterile ether screen being raised into place, Taiga nodded vigorously:
nodes.ar2_s3_15: "Got it! I'm leaving everything to you, Dr. Artoria!"
nodes.ar2_s3_16: Once anesthesia was secure, Artoria and Sakaguchi stepped out to the scrub room and completed a meticulous standard surgical scrub at the sensor sinks.
nodes.ar2_s3_17: As the foot-pedal door slid open, both entered the operating room with hands held high. Beside the instrument table, Miyuki Asakura already stood waiting with sterile towels and unfolded long-sleeved surgical gowns—though Miyuki wasn't among Hoshimi's earliest arrivals and had even double-checked Artoria's preferred liver-parenchyma clamp sizes and ultrasound probe sleeve specs beforehand, the poised veteran fluency with which she presented gowns, gloved hands, and organized her table was a pleasure to watch, while circulating nurse Anji Tonegawa slipped deftly behind them to tie the back straps without touching the sterile front.
nodes.ar2_s3_18: With wide upper-abdominal prep completed and four layers of sterile drapes squared off, the shadowless lamps converged squarely onto the reversed-L incision line marked from the right upper quadrant to beneath the xiphoid.
nodes.ar2_s3_19: "Patient Taiga Fujimura, twenty-five-year-old female, scheduled for elective open left hepatectomy. High thoracic epidural block level stable, blood pressure 116 over 72, heart rate 70—time-out verified!"
nodes.ar2_s3_20: "Beginning the operation. Miyuki, number twenty scalpel."
nodes.ar2_s3_22: The instant the first stroke came down, Sakaguchi's gaze sharpened from across the table at first assistant.
nodes.ar2_s3_23: If Emiko Mido's blade felt like an ice-cold willow knife so swift it stole your breath, the scalpel in Artoria Pendragon's hand moved like a weighted straightedge without half a millimeter of wasted tremor.
nodes.ar2_s3_24: Skin, subcutaneous fat, linea alba, and right anterior rectus sheath parted in steady, fluid succession; as Sakaguchi coagulated and ligated abdominal-wall vessels opposite her, every transition Artoria made between anatomical planes held tissue tension squarely on the clearest fascial line—never yanking for speed, never losing half a second to hesitation.
nodes.ar2_s3_25: After incising the peritoneum and ligating and dividing the round ligament of the liver, right before setting the costal-margin retractor to expose the diaphragmatic dome, Artoria calmly called toward the head of the table:
nodes.ar2_s3_26: "Anji, please let Ms. Fujimura know we are about to elevate and secure the costal margin. She may notice a mild pulling fullness near her diaphragm—it isn't pain, so breathing slowly with it is all she needs to do."
nodes.ar2_s3_27: Anji leaned down at once to relay the message softly, and Taiga's slightly sleepy, muffled reply floated back from behind the drape:
nodes.ar2_s3_28: "Mm... Roger that, doesn't hurt a bit, breathing nice and slow... Cut away, doctors..."
nodes.ar2_s3_29: Under gentle supplemental sedation and dense epidural blockade, the breathing behind the screen soon settled into long, even rhythms.
nodes.ar2_s3_30: With the costal retractor locked solidly in place, Sakaguchi slid warm saline-soaked laparotomy pads smoothly between the visceral surface of the liver and the lesser curvature, shielding the stomach, duodenum, and transverse colon. Smooth dark-red liver and the bulging, full contour of the massive left-lobe mass came cleanly into view at the center of the field.
nodes.ar2_s3_31: Cradling the left lobe gently in her left hand, Artoria worked long-tip electrocautery and fine Metzenbaum scissors along avascular planes to mobilize the falciform, left coronary, and left triangular ligaments—deep beneath the diaphragmatic dome and pericardium, the left triangular ligament hugs the root of the left hepatic vein where a single slip can tear a major venous wall, yet under Artoria's rock-steady wrist both peritoneal leaves parted immaculate and dry, without a single stray bead of dark venous oozing.
nodes.ar2_s3_32: "Perihepatic mobilization complete. First pass of intraoperative ultrasound to verify whole-liver and portal anatomy—Miyuki, sterile probe."
nodes.ar2_s3_33: "High-frequency T-probe double-sleeved in long sterile covers, sterile gel ready—Anji, take the non-sterile console plug."
nodes.ar2_s3_34: "Ultrasound console connected off-field, gain calibrated and normal!"
nodes.ar2_s3_35: Once the initial scan confirmed zero occult lesions in the right hemiliver, the operation entered the true proving ground of hepatobiliary surgery: dissection of the first porta hepatis.
nodes.ar2_s3_36: Rather than resorting to a blunt Pringle clamp shutting off inflow to the entire liver at once, Artoria pre-looped a soft vessel tape around the hepatoduodenal ligament as a safety backup, then took fine right-angle forceps straight through the hilar plate capsule into the umbilical fissure and the root of the left Glissonean pedicle.
nodes.ar2_s3_37: Elevating the inferior edge of segment IV gently with an atraumatic retractor, Sakaguchi watched up close as the hands across from him threaded between delicate caudate portal venules barely millimeters wide and the bifurcation of the left hepatic artery—dissecting, elevating, passing silk ties, double-ligating.
nodes.ar2_s3_38: There was not a shred of flashy theatrics, yet every opening and closing of her forceps tips landed squarely inside the bloodless adventitial plane.
nodes.ar2_s3_39: "Left hepatic artery division confirmed. Main trunk of the left portal vein mobilized, caudate branches preserved intact proximally—applying test clamp."
nodes.ar2_s3_40: Barely a dozen seconds after the atraumatic bulldog clamp clicked shut on the left portal vein, a striking surgical sight unfolded beneath the shadowless lights:
nodes.ar2_s3_41: Across the entire left hemiliver, bright reddish-brown deepened swiftly to dusky violaceous purple, etching a knife-sharp ischemic demarcation line down the junction of left and right while the healthy right hemiliver remained rosy, full, and strongly pulsatile!
nodes.ar2_s3_42: Beside the instrument table, Miyuki Asakura took in that razor-clean line of demarcation, genuine admiration glinting in her eyes above her mask.
nodes.ar2_s3_43: And as superficial-to-mid parenchymal transection began immediately afterward, Sakaguchi set aside the very last trace of underestimation.
nodes.ar2_s3_44: Scoring the capsule with electrocautery two millimeters to the left of the ischemic line, Artoria switched to fine Kelly-clysis parenchymal forceps. With every gentle crush of thin hepatic tissue, her fingertips read each tiny encased vessel and biliary radicle through the steel—coagulating twigs under a millimeter with pinpoint accuracy, and trading small titanium clips or fine silk ligatures seamlessly with Miyuki on anything larger before dividing.
nodes.ar2_s3_45: The parted hepatic cut surface lay as flat and clean as an open book—free of both the welling hemorrhage of reckless haste and the gray devitalized clumps left by crude mass ligatures.
nodes.ar2_s3_46: Watching those astonishingly steady hands across the drape, a single realization crystallized in Sakaguchi's mind—
nodes.ar2_s3_47: Around the hospital, people were fond of calling Emiko Mido "the pinnacle of individual technique" while filing Artoria Pendragon away as "the commander skilled at marshaling formations."
nodes.ar2_s3_48: Only by standing across from her as first assistant on an actual liver resection could anyone understand: this Deputy Chief of Surgery did not emphasize teamwork and structure because her own blade lacked speed or precision. Judged purely by those hands working millimeter by millimeter beside major hilar vessels, she already possessed the top-flight prowess to contend with Mido head-on.
nodes.ar2_s4_01: Parenchymal transection advanced steadily into the mid-to-deep plane, where the pale bluish-white outer wall of the middle hepatic vein trunk began to glimmer along the right side of the cleft.
nodes.ar2_s4_02: At the head of the table, Anji Tonegawa reported quietly:
nodes.ar2_s4_03: "Blood pressure 114 over 70, heart rate 68, oxygen saturation 99 percent, minimal blood loss—the patient is resting peacefully in light sleep."
nodes.ar2_s4_04: True to the checkpoint established in the doctors' office the night before, before advancing deeper toward the mid-segment of the middle hepatic vein and the root of the left hepatic vein, Artoria deliberately paused her forceps and laid a warm saline sponge gently over the cut surface:
nodes.ar2_s4_05: "We are past the halfway depth. Before going deeper, let us run intraoperative ultrasound once more—directly against the cut surface to verify that right anterior venous tributary."
nodes.ar2_s4_06: Miyuki Asakura immediately passed the sterile-sleeved T-probe:
nodes.ar2_s4_08: Artoria nestled the transducer gently against the moist hepatic cut surface. Real-time grayscale B-mode imaging unfolded crisply across the side monitor—to the left lay the intact capsule and uniform echo of the large benign lesion; to the right pulsed the wide lumen of the main middle hepatic vein in rhythm with respiration.
nodes.ar2_s4_09: Keeping his eyes fixed on the center of the screen, Sakaguchi caught sight of the vascular shadow that had looked slightly indistinct on last night's CT the instant the probe tilted two degrees.
nodes.ar2_s4_10: Under unobstructed real-time intraoperative ultrasound, that stout hepatic venous tributary draining a wide territory of healthy right anterior liver bowed gently leftward over its final two centimeters before entering the middle hepatic vein—sitting squarely beneath the downward extension of their planned transection plane!
nodes.ar2_s4_11: Sakaguchi spoke up immediately, his voice low and crisp:
nodes.ar2_s4_12: "Dr. Artoria, hold for a second—if we keep carrying this plane straight down, we'll pass too close to that right anterior venous branch."
nodes.ar2_s4_13: Artoria held the probe rock-steady on that cross-section, her gaze calm and intent:
nodes.ar2_s4_14: "I see it. Less than two millimeters from our projected plane, and its caliber is wider than estimated on CT—it carries nearly all the venous outflow for the upper right anterior sector."
nodes.ar2_s4_15: No one had made an error, nor was there any sudden hemorrhagic crisis. Under a conventional mindset focused solely on "getting the left lobe and lesion out cleanly," a surgeon could simply ligate and divide this inconvenient tributary, finish the operation smoothly, and even save fifteen minutes of delicate dissection—at the price of leaving the anterior margin of Taiga Fujimura's remaining right liver chronically congested and swollen.
nodes.ar2_s4_16: Sakaguchi looked across at the lead surgeon:
nodes.ar2_s4_17: "Are we shifting the deep transection line?"
nodes.ar2_s4_18: Without a flicker of hesitation—or stubborn attachment to the straight line drawn on yesterday's whiteboard—Artoria glided the probe slowly to measure the thickness of normal liver parenchyma between the tributary's left wall and the lesion's intact pseudocapsule:
nodes.ar2_s4_19: "Reconfirming resection margin—look at the left side of the screen: there are still a full eight millimeters or more of normal hepatic parenchyma outside the lesion's pseudocapsule. Because this is a benign mass with an intact capsule, we can shift this deep segment five millimeters leftward without breaching the capsule or compromising complete excision, hugging the left wall of the tributary so the entire outflow channel stays intact with the right liver."
nodes.ar2_s4_20: "We can adjust the route, without changing the objective of the operation."
nodes.ar2_s4_21: Two concise sentences laid out both why the line could move and exactly how far it could go.
nodes.ar2_c2a_01: Catching her intent at once, Sakaguchi shifted his left-hand traction on the specimen side from lateral pull to a gentle upward-left lift—unloading lateral tension off the tributary's wall—while his right-hand saline-drip suction tip cleared trace oozing along the cleft to bring the pale-blue venous adventitia into crystal-clear relief:
nodes.ar2_c2a_02: "Left-side tension is off, and the vein wall isn't collapsing under pull—you have a clean extrafascial plane."
nodes.ar2_c2a_03: Approval flickered in Artoria's eyes as her fine dissection forceps glided steadily into the plane he opened:
nodes.ar2_c2a_04: "Traction angle is spot-on. Hold that exact feel, Dr. Sakaguchi."
nodes.ar2_c2b_01: Maintaining exposure with one hand, Sakaguchi took the fine bipolar forceps before the probe came off the liver, lightly dotting three superficial reference points along the left cleft margin matched to the ultrasound depth:
nodes.ar2_c2b_02: "Keeping safe thickness outside the capsule, curving five millimeters left through these three marks past the confluence before rejoining the left hepatic vein root plane—does that depth line up?"
nodes.ar2_c2b_03: Scanning the three dead-accurate reference marks, Artoria lifted the probe decisively and handed it back to Miyuki:
nodes.ar2_c2b_04: "Down to the millimeter. Having you cross-check spatial geometry across the table saves a great deal of repeated verification."
nodes.ar2_c2c_01: Reading the anatomical layers along the shifted path, Sakaguchi quietly alerted both the scrub table and the lead surgeon:
nodes.ar2_c2c_02: "Hugging the left wall of this tributary means we'll meet two or three tiny bridging venules draining from segment IV into it. Miyuki, have 5-0 vascular sutures and micro-forceps ready up front."
nodes.ar2_c2c_03: Miyuki immediately slid the pre-loaded fine needle holder into the front handover slot:
nodes.ar2_c2c_04: "5-0 polypropylene and atraumatic micro-forceps standing by."
nodes.ar2_c2c_05: "Well spotted. We will ligate each of those tiny branches flush with the wall one by one—no electrocautery thermal spread near the main trunk."
nodes.ar2_s4r_01: The fifteen minutes that followed formed the technical crescendo of the entire open hepatic lobectomy.
nodes.ar2_s4r_02: Deep at the floor of a parenchymal cleft several centimeters down, Artoria Pendragon wielded fine dissection forceps and micro-needle holder in person, advancing millimeter by millimeter along the revised arc toward the second porta hepatis.
nodes.ar2_s4r_03: Confronting two gossamer venules narrower than a millimeter entering the side wall of the right anterior tributary directly, her fingertips did not waver a hair—tying 5-0 suture flush on the proximal side without narrowing the parent lumen, seating a micro-titanium clip distally, and dividing between them without losing a single drop of blood.
nodes.ar2_s4r_04: When the left Glissonean pedicle stump and the root of the left hepatic vein were secured in turn under direct vision with suture-ligation and atraumatic linear closure, and the entire left hemiliver specimen cradling the massive mass was lifted smoothly into Miyuki Asakura's sterile basin, the healthy liver remaining on the right presented a textbook sight—
nodes.ar2_s4r_05: The full trunk of the middle hepatic vein together with its stout right anterior tributary lay intact and plump along the smooth cut surface, while the remnant right liver gleamed an even arterial red without the faintest dusky patch of venous congestion along its margin!
nodes.ar2_s4r_06: Artoria did not relax a fraction just because the specimen was out. Taking a clean, dry white gauze pad from Miyuki, she laid it gently across the entire hepatic cut surface and around the hilar bile duct stump, waited half a minute in silence, then lifted it toward the light to inspect:
nodes.ar2_s4r_07: "Zero yellow staining on the white gauze—no bile leak from the right hepatic duct or cut-surface radicles; hemostasis across the raw surface is complete, and arterial pulsation, portal filling, and venous outflow in the remnant right liver are all normal."
nodes.ar2_s4r_08: Sakaguchi irrigated the subphrenic and subhepatic spaces thoroughly with warm saline; once the return ran crystal clear, he withdrew each warm saline protective pad from above the lesser curvature and duodenum back to the counting area and seated a closed abdominal drain beside the right subphrenic cut surface.
nodes.ar2_s4r_09: "Pre-closure count—all warm saline abdominal laparotomy pads removed; sponges, pledgets, vascular clamps, needles, and all instruments verified correct on dual count with Anji!"
nodes.ar2_s4r_10: "Circulating log verified on dual count—all counts correct!"
nodes.ar2_s4r_11: Peritoneum, anterior and posterior rectus sheaths, and subcutis came together layer by neat layer between the two surgeons; as Miyuki and Anji called out "final closing count verified correct," the last skin suture knotted crisply and sterile dressings were smoothed into place.
nodes.ar2_s4r_12: As the sterile screen came down, Taiga Fujimura blinked awake from light sleep, looking between Anji's warm smile and the lead surgeon stripping off her outer gloves beside the table as she asked softly:
nodes.ar2_s4r_14: Stepping to the side of the table, Artoria answered gently and clearly through her mask:
nodes.ar2_s4r_15: "The operation went very smoothly, Ms. Fujimura. The lesion has been completely removed, and the part of your liver that remains was protected very well."
nodes.ar2_s4r_16: Warmth stung the rims of Taiga's eyes as she broke into a radiant, deeply relieved smile:
nodes.ar2_s4r_17: "...Thank goodness! Thank you so much, Dr. Artoria—and thank you too, Dr. Sakaguchi and nurses!"
nodes.ar2_s5_01: After escorting Taiga Fujimura safely back to her ward bed, settling her onto monitors, and verifying clear, minimal first-hour drain output, Sakaguchi changed back into his white coat and walked into the quiet afternoon surgical doctors' office.
nodes.ar2_s5_02: It was just past one-thirty; most of the day-shift surgeons had headed to the cafeteria or outpatient clinics, leaving only Artoria Pendragon seated with impeccable posture at her usual desk in the office, carefully annotating today's ultrasound-verified venous course onto the operative note diagram with her fountain pen.
nodes.ar2_s5_03: Walking over, Sakaguchi glanced at the sketch mapping the middle hepatic vein and right anterior tributary and asked:
nodes.ar2_s5_04: "Dr. Artoria, back in stage four when you saw that right anterior tributary bowing leftward, it took you less than a minute to shift the deep transection line five millimeters left. In a radical cancer resection where margin can't give ground—or if that tributary hugged the capsule itself—where would you draw the line?"
nodes.ar2_s5_05: Capping her pen's pause, Artoria looked up and slid the diagram halfway toward him as naturally as speaking with a true peer:
nodes.ar2_s5_06: "That is precisely why lesion pathology, margin rules, and remnant liver reserve must be calculated together beforehand. Because Ms. Fujimura's mass today was a benign hyperplasia with an intact pseudocapsule—needing no extra one-to-two-centimeter cuff of normal liver—yielding five millimeters toward the capsule compromised zero percent of our curative goal while sparing smooth outflow to nearly twenty percent of her remnant liver."
nodes.ar2_s5_07: She touched the tip of her pen lightly to the right half of the sketch representing the preserved liver:
nodes.ar2_s5_08: "Conversely, if we face a malignant tumor demanding a wide margin where that tributary must be sacrificed, then preoperative planning has to evaluate compensatory collateral drainage through the right posterior sector as well—confirming that effective functional remnant volume still clears the safety threshold after sacrificing it, or else refusing to force the resection as originally drawn."
nodes.ar2_s5_09: Looking down at the steady arc curving around the venous tributary on the page, Sakaguchi suddenly understood to the core what she had told Taiga Fujimura at the bedside yesterday afternoon.
nodes.ar2_s5_10: When many surgeons stand beneath the shadowless lights, what they see is a duel between surgeon and lesion—the faster it comes out and the cleaner the cut, the more decisively they feel they have won;
nodes.ar2_s5_11: When Artoria Pendragon stood at that exact same table, what remained in her sights from start to finish was the living person after the last stitch closed—the person who still had to go back to working, eating, and swinging a bamboo sword in her dojo with the organ left inside her.
nodes.ar2_s5_12: What is removed is merely today's task on the table; what remains is what truly shapes the rest of the patient's life.
nodes.ar2_s5_13: Seeing Sakaguchi deep in thought, Artoria capped her fountain pen with a warm expression and slid a neatly organized clinical handout across the desk toward him—Open Hepatic Lobectomy: Essentials of Inflow Control and Intraoperative Ultrasound Transection Navigation:
nodes.ar2_s5_14: "Your exposure control, tension judgment at first assistant, and timely callout during intraoperative ultrasound today were all exemplary, Dr. Sakaguchi."
nodes.ar2_s5_15: "With the surgical foundation you already possess, once you internalize cut-surface Glissonean/venous identification and remnant outflow assessment, you are fully capable of serving as lead surgeon on open hepatic lobectomies in the regular schedule. Take these departmental technical notes first—we can continue comparing notes on upcoming cases."
nodes.ar2_s5_16: Sakaguchi accepted the handout with genuine respect:
nodes.ar2_s5_17: "Thank you for the guidance, Dr. Artoria. Today's case genuinely taught me a great deal."
nodes.ar2_s5_19: "Likewise. Having a partner as steady as you across the table makes the lead surgeon's burden far lighter."
nodes.ar2_s5_20: Hardly pausing half a minute to catch her breath after saying so, she reached straight for tomorrow morning's surgical bed-turnover sheet atop her inbox stack and uncapped her fountain pen again.
nodes.ar2_s5_21: Just then, Sakaguchi's gaze fell on the white porcelain teacup beside her hand—black tea steeped right after morning handover, its surface long devoid of steam, chilled to the core. Glancing up at the wall clock, the minute hand had already passed one-forty in the afternoon.
nodes.ar2_s5_22: Nearly four hours standing through a major open hepatectomy, escorting the patient back, then writing up an exhaustive operative record and review diagram without a break...
nodes.ar2_s5_23: Watching her crisp profile bent intently over the roster, Sakaguchi asked out of nowhere:
nodes.ar2_s5_24: "Dr. Artoria—you haven't had lunch yet, have you?"
nodes.ar2_s5_25: Artoria's fingers paused on the sheet; she looked up and answered with complete deadpan gravity:
nodes.ar2_s5_26: "I still have a small amount of work."
nodes.ar2_s5_27: Sakaguchi pointed between the wall clock and the stone-cold cup of black tea:
nodes.ar2_s5_28: "Meaning you haven't eaten a single bite since morning."
nodes.ar2_s5_30: The deputy chief who had just displayed master-class hepatobiliary command at the operating table fell silent for a full two seconds; without a trace of guilt on her poised fair face, she offered an utterly earnest defense:
nodes.ar2_s5_31: "Those two facts do not contradict one another."
nodes.ar2_s5_32: It was pure sophistry, yet delivered in that impeccably upright, dead-serious tone of hers, it carried an endearing contrast impossible to get mad at.
nodes.ar2_c3a_01: Holding back a grin, Sakaguchi lifted the liver-resection handout he had just received:
nodes.ar2_c3a_02: "A certain lead surgeon lectured me less than ten minutes ago about not fixating on finishing the task while neglecting 'the functional reserve left behind'—so how come the deputy chief's own physical reserve gets left unprotected?"
nodes.ar2_c3a_03: Artoria blinked faintly, clearly caught off guard to have her own clinical principle turned right back on her.
nodes.ar2_c3a_04: At that exact instant, an exceedingly faint—yet unmistakable—growl echoed through the quiet doctors' office.
nodes.ar2_c3a_05: The rim of Artoria's ear tinted the faintest shade of pink; clearing her throat softly around her fountain pen, she closed the bed-turnover folder with dignified precision:
nodes.ar2_c3a_06: "...You make a fair point. Maintaining adequate physical reserve is indeed part of a clinician's professional duty. As soon as I finish checking this page, I will go get something to eat."
nodes.ar2_c3b_01: Glancing at his watch, Sakaguchi turned casually toward the office door:
nodes.ar2_c3b_02: "The staff cafeteria has probably wrapped up lunch service by now, though the first-floor kiosk restocks warm sandwiches and beef croquettes in the afternoon. I'm heading downstairs for lunch myself—mind if I bring a set up for you?"
nodes.ar2_c3b_03: At the words "warm sandwiches and beef croquettes," Artoria's emerald eyes lit up for the briefest fraction of a second before she composed herself and politely reached into her white-coat pocket for her coin purse:
nodes.ar2_c3b_04: "...I would appreciate that, Dr. Sakaguchi. If it isn't any trouble, one sandwich and one croquette please—let me give you the money first."
nodes.ar2_c3b_05: Sakaguchi waved a hand with a chuckle:
nodes.ar2_c3b_06: "Settle up with me after you've eaten your fill."
nodes.ar2_c3c_01: Sakaguchi glanced at the porcelain cup beside her hand:
nodes.ar2_c3c_02: "That black tea has been sitting there since before morning rounds, hasn't it? Even an ironclad deputy chief can't power through an entire floor of afternoon post-op rounds on half a cup of cold tea."
nodes.ar2_c3c_03: Looking down at the undeniably undrinkable cold tea, Artoria shifted her gaze aside with a hint of sheepishness:
nodes.ar2_c3c_04: "...I became absorbed verifying the ultrasound notes and lost track of the hour. Thank you for the reminder, Dr. Sakaguchi—I will head down to the first floor for a light meal right away."
nodes.ar2_s5r_01: Gathering the annotated operative files neatly into a folder, Artoria stood up to carry the cold teacup over to the pantry sink, her posture as upright, composed, and unflagging as ever.
nodes.ar2_s5r_02: Standing by the sunlit doorway of the doctors' office, Sakaguchi glanced down at the crisp, resolute handwriting on the Open Hepatic Lobectomy handout in his hand, the corner of his mouth lifting slightly.
nodes.ar2_s5r_03: So this Deputy Chief of Surgery who always sat at the center of the office coordinating the big picture didn't merely know how to forge ten clinicians into a single unit—the moment she stepped into the primary surgeon's spot and took up the blade herself, that blend of keenness and restraint was just as formidable.
nodes.ar2_s5r_04: As for her little habit of forgetting meals completely once absorbed in work—for now it seemed a harmless enough quirk, one there would be plenty of time to keep an eye on in the working days ahead.
